trials.notes: Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() and used only documented methods. The token walk uses documented text/depth primitives, but the state machine flushes the current heading on any descendant tag opener before checking whether it is another heading. That breaks the documented subtree-text pattern and caused the 5/7 result.

Correct processor and all API calls are documented. The closer-driven single token loop is idiomatic and handles decoded text, empty headings, inline markup, and implied heading closes. Minor issue: heading detection via string range is less precise than an explicit H1-H6 set and could include non-heading tag names such as H10.

Correct processor and all API calls are documented. Uses the documented depth-boundary model and #text/get_modifiable_text pattern well, including empty and implied-closed headings. Returning an empty result on get_last_error() is a defensible fail-closed policy, though the task did not require an unsupported-input policy.

failure_analysis: Failed cases were both in trial-1. In basic-h1-h3 it returned "Details " instead of "Details here" because it treated the nested EM opener as ending the H3. In nested-text-and-entities it returned "A " instead of "A B & C" for the same reason with SPAN. The misconception is that an opener inside a heading means the heading has been implicitly closed; actual HTML Processor behavior is that descendant inline tags remain inside the heading until the heading closer/depth drop. The relevant docs are present but were not transferred: html-processor.md, "Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree" says to append only #text tokens reached by the subtree walk and notes inline markup can split text across tokens; "next_token()" says an element's text may be split across several #text tokens and gives a strong-in-LI example; "get_current_depth()" explains that the subtree guard must continue while depth is >= the opener depth. The docs prevented hallucinated API use across all trials, but trial-1 shows a gap in making the subtree termination rule salient for inline descendants and repeated region state machines.

doc_gaps.location: html-processor.md: Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree
doc_gaps.problem: The recipe is correct but generic; a reader still generalized incorrectly that a nested opener can terminate the current text-containing element.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short warning after the example: descendant openers such as EM, SPAN, A, or STRONG do not end the ancestor being scanned; only the ancestor closer, a virtual closer, or a depth drop below the recorded opener depth ends the subtree.

doc_gaps.problem: The one-pass state-machine example demonstrates closer-driven flushing, but not the common case of collecting repeated text-bearing elements while allowing arbitrary inline descendants.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a task-neutral example for repeated subtree text extraction, such as collecting text for each matched element name from a set, where the code classifies a new region opener before flushing and ignores non-region descendant openers.

doc_gaps.problem: The >= depth rule is documented, but the consequence for opening child tags is implicit.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Include a compact token/depth table for an inline-markup subtree, e.g. an element containing text, STRONG, more text, showing that the child opener and child text remain within the ancestor boundary.
